# Hamming Protocol-Core ISA

Canonical 16-bit instruction set and CSR map for the four Hamming
protocol cores. This file is generated from `tools/hamming_isa.py`;
the assembler (`tools/hamming_asm.py`) and Golden ISS
(`tools/hamming_iss.py`) share the same tables.

## Machine model

- Four 16-bit GPRs `r0`-`r3`, 10-bit PC (1024 x 16-bit
  instruction slots in SRAM 0), flags `Z` `C` `EQ`, sticky
  `deadline_missed`, private 4-bit `core_out`/`core_oe` pin channel,
  private 20-bit `anchor`.
- Shared free-running 20-bit global `timer` and atomic
  `EV_FLAGS[7:0]` (cores wait/jump on `EV_FLAGS[3:0]`).
- SRAM 0: 512 x 32-bit (code + tables, 2 instructions per
  word). SRAM 1: 512 x 32-bit data. Loop cache:
  8 x 32-bit direct-mapped lines keyed by SRAM 0 word
  address; hit = 1 cycle, miss = 3..7
  cycles. SRAM 1 reads 3..8 cycles, write
  grant <= 6 cycles.

## Major opcodes `[15:12]`

| Major | Group | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x0 | ALU | `[11:8]` alu_op, `[7:6]` rd, `[5:4]` rs, `[3:0]`=0 |
| 0x1 | LDI8 | `[11:10]` rd, `[9:8]` half, `[7:0]` imm8 |
| 0x2 | PIN | `[11:8]` sub, see PIN table |
| 0x3 | TIMING | `[11:8]` sub, see TIMING table |
| 0x4 | BCU | `[11:8]` sub, see BCU table |
| 0x5 | MEM | `[11:8]` sub, `[7:6]` ra, `[5:4]` imm2, `[3:2]` rt |
| 0x6 | CSR_RD | `[11:10]` rd, `[9:8]`=0, `[7:0]` csr_addr |
| 0x7 | CSR_WR | `[11:10]` rs, `[9:8]`=0, `[7:0]` csr_addr |
| 0x8 | JMP | `[11:10]`=0, `[9:0]` pc10 |
| 0x9 | BR | `[11:10]` kind (JZ/JNZ/JEV/CALL) |
| 0xA | MISC | `[11:8]` sub (RET/HALT/NOP), `[7:0]`=0 |
| 0xB-0xF | reserved | rejected by the assembler |

## ALU sub-ops (major 0x0)

`rd`/`rs` select `r0`-`r3`. `Z` = (result == 0). `C` = carry-out
for `add`/`shl`, borrow for `sub`/`cmp`, bit shifted out for `shr`;
unchanged otherwise. `EQ` is written by `cmp` only.

| alu_op | Mnemonic | Operands | Semantics | Flags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x0 | mov | rd, rs | rd <= rs | Z |
| 0x1 | add | rd, rs | rd <= rd + rs | Z, C=carry |
| 0x2 | sub | rd, rs | rd <= rd - rs | Z, C=borrow |
| 0x3 | and | rd, rs | rd <= rd & rs | Z |
| 0x4 | or | rd, rs | rd <= rd \| rs | Z |
| 0x5 | xor | rd, rs | rd <= rd ^ rs | Z |
| 0x6 | shl | rd | rd <= rd << 1 | Z, C=old bit15 |
| 0x7 | shr | rd | rd <= rd >> 1 | Z, C=old bit0 |
| 0x8 | cmp | rd, rs | compare rd - rs (rd unchanged) | Z, C=borrow, EQ=(rd==rs) |
| 0x9 | not | rd, rs | rd <= ~rs | Z |
| 0xA | inc | rd | rd <= rd + 1 | Z |
| 0xB | dec | rd | rd <= rd - 1 | Z |

## LDI8 (major 0x1)

`ldi8.l rd, imm8` loads `rd[7:0]`; `ldi8.h rd, imm8` loads
`rd[15:8]`. The other byte is preserved. Flags unchanged.

## PIN sub-ops (major 0x2)

| sub | Mnemonic | Fields | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | pin_out | `[7:4]` mask4, `[3:0]` val4 | core_out <= (core_out & ~mask4) \| (val4 & mask4) |
| 1 | pin_oe | `[7:4]` mask4, `[3:0]` val4 | core_oe <= (core_oe & ~mask4) \| (val4 & mask4) |
| 2 | pin_in | `[7:4]` pin 0-15, `[3:2]` rd | rd <= synced pin input bit |
| 3 | lut_read | `[7:4]` lut 0-15, `[3:2]` rd | rd <= LUT[lut] output bit |

## TIMING sub-ops (major 0x3)

| sub | Mnemonic | Fields | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | wait_phase rs | `[3:2]` rs | deadline = anchor + rs; stall until timer reaches it |
| 1 | wait_phase imm8 | `[7:0]` imm8 | deadline = anchor + imm8; stall until timer reaches it |
| 2 | sync_event | `[7:4]` ev_mask4, `[3:2]` timeout reg | wait for EV_FLAGS[3:0]&mask, up to reg cycles; re-anchor on wake/timeout |
| 3 | set_anchor | `[7:0]` imm8 | anchor <= timer + imm8 |
| 4 | read_timer | `[7:4]` sel, `[3:2]` rd | sel 0: rd <= timer[15:0]; sel 1: rd <= {deadline_missed, 11'b0, timer[19:16]} |

### Deadline semantics (WAIT_PHASE / SYNC_EVENT)

`deadline = (anchor + delta) mod 2^20`. The core stalls until
`signed20(timer - deadline) >= 0` (i.e. `~diff[19]`). If the
deadline is already strictly in the past at issue (overshoot),
sticky `deadline_missed` is set and the instruction does not
stall; a deadline equal to the current timer is exactly on time
(no stall, no miss). Legal `delta` is 0..524287 (signed half-range);
`set_anchor` renews the anchor. `sync_event` waits for
`(EV_FLAGS[3:0] & mask) != 0` for up to `timeout` reg cycles,
then re-anchors to the wakeup cycle (`anchor <= timer`) whether
it woke on an event or timed out.

## BCU sub-ops (major 0x4)

| sub | Mnemonic | Fields | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | bcu_tx | `[3:2]` rs | push rs into BCU TX shadow |
| 1 | bcu_rx | `[3:2]` rd | rd <= BCU RX shadow |
| 2 | bcu_ctrl | `[7:0]` imm8 | BCU control strobe byte |
| 3 | bcu_stat | `[3:2]` rd | rd <= BCU status word |
| 4 | bcu_crc_rd | `[7:6]` sel, `[3:2]` rd | rd <= crc_state[15:0] (sel=0) or [31:16] (sel=1) |

### BCU status bits

| Bit | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | crc_ok | CRC residue check passed |
| 1 | rx_eop_done | RX end-of-packet / frame delimiter seen |
| 2 | sfd_match | SFD / pattern matcher hit |
| 3 | stuff_err | bit-stuffing rule violation |
| 4 | tx_empty | TX shadow buffer empty |
| 5 | rx_full | RX shadow buffer full |

## MEM sub-ops (major 0x5)

Effective address `ea = rs[ra] + imm2`. Word ops address the
512 x 32-bit SRAM 1 word `ea & 0x1FF`. Byte ops use
`word = (ea >> 2) & 0x1FF`, lane `ea & 3`. `ld_imem` reads the
SRAM 0 tables region: 16-bit entry index `ea` selects
halfword `ea & 1` of word `ea >> 1`.

| sub | Mnemonic | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | ld_dmem_w | rt <= SRAM1[ea & 0x1FF] |
| 1 | st_dmem_w | SRAM1[ea & 0x1FF] <= rt |
| 2 | ld_dmem_b | rt <= byte lane ea[1:0] of SRAM1[ea>>2] |
| 3 | st_dmem_b | byte lane ea[1:0] of SRAM1[ea>>2] <= rt[7:0] |
| 4 | ld_imem | rt <= SRAM0 16-bit entry ea (tables) |

## CSR access (majors 0x6 / 0x7)

`csr_rd rd, addr` / `csr_wr rs, addr`, 8-bit address, 16-bit data,
1 cycle, never stalls. Core `k` may only write its private bank
`0x40 + k*16 .. +0xF` plus the atomic `EV_SET`/`EV_CLR` CSRs;
writes outside the owned set are dropped.

### Global CSRs (0x00-0x1F)

| Addr | Name | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x00 | CTRL_RUN | [3:0] atomic core start mask |
| 0x01 | EV_FLAGS | read EV_FLAGS[7:0] |
| 0x02 | EV_SET | atomic EV_FLAGS \|= wdata |
| 0x03 | EV_CLR | atomic EV_FLAGS &= ~wdata |
| 0x04 | TIMER_LO | read timer[15:0] |
| 0x05 | TIMER_HI | read {11'b0, timer[19:16]} |
| 0x06 | RLE_BASE | RLE ring base word address |
| 0x07 | RLE_MASK | RLE ring power-of-two mask |
| 0x08 | RLE_WR_PTR | RLE ring write pointer |
| 0x09 | RLE_STATUS | bit0 overflow, bit1 underflow, bit2 capturing |
| 0x0A | PIN_FILT_EN | per-pin 4-tap glitch filter enable |
| 0x0B | OPEN_DRAIN_EN | post-router open-drain clamp |
| 0x0C | RLE_CTRL | mode, trig en/sel, sticky clear |
| 0x0D | RLE_PROBE_MASK | edge-detect arm mask for probe[15:0] |
| 0x20 | PIN_ROUTER0 | output pin router channels 3:0 |
| 0x21 | PIN_ROUTER1 | output pin router channels 7:4 |
| 0x22 | PIN_ROUTER2 | output pin router channels 11:8 |
| 0x23 | PIN_ROUTER3 | output pin router channels 15:12 |
| 0x24 | PIN_ROUTER4 | output pin router channels 19:16 |
| 0x25 | PIN_ROUTER5 | output pin router channels 22:20 |

| Offset | Name | Notes |

### LUT matrix CSRs (0x80-0xAF)

| Addr | Name | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0x80-0x8F | LUT_TT[k] | 16-bit truth table for LUT k (k=0..15) |
| 0x90-0x9F | LUT_SEL[k] | four 4-bit input selectors for LUT k |
| 0xA0 | LUT_OREG | bit k: LUT k output register enable |

## Control flow (majors 0x8 / 0x9 / 0xA)

| Mnemonic | Encoding | Semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jmp pc10 | 0x8, `[9:0]` pc10 | pc <= pc10 |
| jz pc10 | 0x9 kind 0, `[9:0]` pc10 | pc <= pc10 if Z |
| jnz pc10 | 0x9 kind 1, `[9:0]` pc10 | pc <= pc10 if !Z |
| jev mask, rs | 0x9 kind 2, `[9:6]` mask4, `[3:2]` rs | pc <= rs & 0x3FF if (EV_FLAGS[3:0] & mask4) != 0 |
| call pc10 | 0x9 kind 3, `[9:0]` pc10 | push pc+1 onto 2-deep return stack; pc <= pc10 |
| ret | 0xA sub 0 | pc <= pop return stack (empty: pc <= 0) |
| halt | 0xA sub 1 | core enters HALTED; timer keeps running |
| nop | 0xA sub 2 | no operation |

Branches have no delay slot. Return stack overflow drops the
oldest entry.

## Cycle costs (Golden ISS)

| Operation | Cycles |
| --- | --- |
| Any instruction, loop-cache hit | 1 total (fetch+execute) |
| Any instruction, loop-cache miss | 3..7 total (default 4) |
| ld_dmem_*/ld_imem extra | SRAM1: 3..8 (default 5); SRAM0 tables: same as miss |
| st_dmem_* extra | write grant <= 6 (default 3) |
| csr_rd / csr_wr | no extra cycles |
| wait_phase | stall = (deadline - timer) mod 2^20 cycles |
| sync_event | stall = cycles until event or timeout |
